run.question:
I'm connected to the ci-cd cluster. We got a P1 alert and need help finding the root cause.
Our cluster inventory is in the app-235-cluster-inventory index and deployment/change history
is in the app-235-change-history index. Please search these indices to investigate.
[
  {
    "annotations": {
      "description": "Online Devices count gradual decrease over 8 hours in [clientorg-alpha] [56%] for over 30m",
      "workload": "clientorg-alpha"
    },
    "fingerprint": "xx1234567890abcd",
    "labels": {
      "alertname": "onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease",
      "app": "lambda-dashboard-monitoring",
      "cluster": "us-prod-eks",
      "grafana_dashboard_name": "Production-Performance-Overview",
      "org": "clientorg-alpha",
      "severity": "critical",
      "slack_channel": "sre-alerts-channel"
    },
    "startsAt": "30 minutes ago",
    "status": "firing"
  }
]
The alert started right after a deployment. Can you check what's the root cause?

report.summary: The alert payload describes a critical `onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease` for workload `clientorg-alpha`, app `lambda-dashboard-monitoring`, cluster `us-prod-eks`. The two indices I was asked to search exist and were read in full for the authorized window, but they describe only the `ci-cd` cluster: the four in-window change-history documents are a `gitlab-runner` scale (BUILD-5PW2K6, 2→3 replicas, namespace `ci`, 2026-11-23T15:59:50Z), an `argocd-server` security patch, a `jenkins` LTS bump and a `flux-controller` config update, and the five in-window cluster-inventory documents are `gitlab-runner`, `jenkins`, `argocd-server`, `tekton-pipelines` and `flux-controller`, all reported Running. No document in either index names `lambda-dashboard-monitoring`, `clientorg-alpha` or `us-prod-eks`, so the deployment the alert says preceded the problem is not recorded in these indices. The live Kubernetes target I can read is a single kind cluster (node `opspilot-m1-control-plane`) whose 24 deployments are only in kube-system, local-path-storage and otel-demo; all 32 pods are Running/ready with restartCount 0 and no last-termination reason, the otel-demo fault-injection flags in `flagd-config` all default to `off`, and the local Prometheus alerting rules contain no `onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease` rule. Prometheus and Jaeger queries all came back unavailable (recorded in gaps, not as evidence), so no metric or trace signal — including the online-device series or any ERROR series — could be checked. I therefore could not identify a root cause: the change that triggered this alert is not present in the available data, and the sole change near the alert window (the gitlab-runner scale-up) belongs to a different application and cluster and is not evidence of impact on the alerting workload.

claims.text: The connected Elasticsearch target holds exactly two indices, both green and open: app-235-change-history (4 documents, 9.7kb) and app-235-cluster-inventory (6 documents, 8.4kb).

app-235-change-history contains exactly 4 documents inside the authorized window (timestamp filtered), all in cluster ci-cd: gitlab-runner change BUILD-5PW2K6, change_type scale, namespace ci, 'Scaled gitlab-runner from 2 to 3 replicas for faster pipeline throughput', 2026-11-23T15:59:50Z; argocd-server BUILD-3NR8Y1 security patch to v2.9.3, 2026-11-23T12:59:50Z; jenkins BUILD-7X4Q9M LTS bump to 2.426.3-lts, 2026-11-23T11:59:50Z; flux-controller BUILD-9TL6V3 config-update (sync interval 5m→3m), 2026-11-16T17:59:50Z. None of these documents names app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, workload clientorg-alpha or cluster us-prod-eks.

app-235-cluster-inventory returns 5 documents inside the window, all cluster ci-cd and all status Running: gitlab-runner (gitlab/gitlab-runner:v16.7.0, namespace ci, 3 replicas, last_updated 2026-11-23T15:59:50Z), jenkins (jenkins/jenkins:2.426.3-lts, ci, 1 replica), argocd-server (quay.io/argoproj/argocd:v2.9.3, ci, 2 replicas), tekton-pipelines (cd, 1 replica) and flux-controller (cd, 1 replica). No inventory entry named lambda-dashboard-monitoring or in namespace clientorg-alpha is present.

The readable Kubernetes cluster has 24 deployments in only three namespaces — kube-system, local-path-storage and otel-demo (the OpenTelemetry demo: ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, jaeger, kube-state-metrics, load-generator, otel-collector, payment, product-catalog, prometheus, prometheus-readonly-proxy, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart) — each with its expected replicas available; there is no deployment for lambda-dashboard-monitoring and no ci/cd namespace in this cluster.

All 32 pods in the readable cluster are phase Running, all containers ready=true, every container restartCount is 0 and every lastState.terminated reason is null — no crash, OOMKill or back-off is visible on any pod in this cluster.

The otel-demo fault-injection ConfigMap flagd-config declares 11 flags (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) and every one of them has defaultVariant "off", i.e. no fault, error, delay or failure setting is switched on in this cluster.

The Prometheus ConfigMap in namespace otel-demo carries alerting rules CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh (checkout PlaceOrder span error ratio > 0.5), OpsPilotAgentAbsent and OpsPilotModelCallsFailing, plus an empty recording_rules.yml; there is no onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease rule and no lambda-dashboard-monitoring related rule in it.

The cluster's ConfigMap inventory (20 ConfigMaps) contains no configuration object referencing lambda-dashboard-monitoring, clientorg-alpha or us-prod-eks; the only application config objects are otel-demo's alertmanager, flagd-config, otel-collector, product-catalog-products and prometheus.

Hypothesis that the gitlab-runner scale from 2 to 3 replicas (BUILD-5PW2K6, 2026-11-23T15:59:50Z) is the deployment the alert followed and the cause of the online-device decline: rejected, because that change is a replica scale of gitlab-runner in namespace ci of cluster ci-cd described as a pipeline-throughput improvement, it changes no configuration of lambda-dashboard-monitoring/clientorg-alpha, and no evidence ties it to online-device counts.

The change that preceded the alert took place in cluster us-prod-eks on app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, which is neither the cluster nor the application recorded in app-235-change-history/app-235-cluster-inventory; this would explain why no matching deployment appears in the searched indices, but it is unverified because no source in this Run covers us-prod-eks.

Obtain change/deployment history for cluster us-prod-eks and app lambda-dashboard-monitoring (the indices searched here only cover ci-cd) and compare the deployment timestamp with the start of the online-device decline, roughly 30 minutes before 2026-11-23T18:00:02Z, before attributing a cause.

Query the online-device gauge for org clientorg-alpha and any lambda/API error and duration series over the hours before 2026-11-23T18:00:02Z once the us-prod-eks monitoring stack is reachable; the only Prometheus rules visible in the readable cluster (CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh, OpsPilotAgentAbsent, OpsPilotModelCallsFailing) contain no onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease rule, so that rule is evaluated outside this cluster.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable throughout this Run: execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names and list_prometheus_rules each returned an error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (operations 8653bb07-6c4f-4663-8d53-955f911691f9, a531a568-2bcb-4cc8-97d0-36ebd867f4f4, d7668ac4-d578-4b32-a9ac-56b10e259327). The online-device series, any ERROR series and any latency baseline were therefore not observed; their values are unknown, not zero, and no latency trend can be claimed.

Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services and traces_search on frontend returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (operations 8653bb07-6c4f-4663-8d53-955f911691f9 and d7668ac4-d578-4b32-a9ac-56b10e259327), so no span-level error or call-path evidence exists in this Run.

The cluster-wide Kubernetes event query returned no_data (view 28fdae20-2de3-4ccc-9e87-861c69cba2a9-t1:5c7d7fb4-5984-4eeb-aec3-dd49b7424ab8); events were not observed either way, so no event-based cause or clearance can be established.

Exact-name searches for app_name lambda-dashboard-monitoring, cluster us-prod-eks and namespace clientorg-alpha in app-235-change-history and app-235-cluster-inventory returned no_data (views fb0cc46e-512e-402c-8d21-d8895eaac672-t0:71f2ee8a-667e-4bf4-a4d2-afa961ef0229 and fb0cc46e-512e-402c-8d21-d8895eaac672-t1:5d27308b-4e61-4d24-9a00-98f66c0956b0); those queries matched nothing in the window, so the alerting workload's deployment record is simply not in these indices rather than proven absent from the environment.

app-235-cluster-inventory holds 6 documents but only 5 fall inside the authorized window 2026-10-24T18:00:02Z–2026-11-23T18:00:02Z, so one inventory document lies outside the window and its content is unknown.
The change-history integration is listed as not_integrated in this Run's data_sources, so no pipeline or release metadata beyond the app-235-change-history documents was available.
Which object, if any, changed in cluster us-prod-eks around the alert onset remains unknown; no root cause can be named from the available evidence.
next_steps: Fetch the deployment/change record for app lambda-dashboard-monitoring in cluster us-prod-eks (for example from that cluster's CD system or its own change-history index) and compare it with the alert onset.

Once the us-prod-eks monitoring stack is reachable, query the onlineDevicesCount metric for org clientorg-alpha and any lambda/API error and duration series over the 8 hours before 2026-11-23T18:00:02Z to locate the deviation start.
Check whether the onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease alert depends on a dashboard query, data source or exporter that the recent deployment may have changed.
Confirm with the infra-team whether BUILD-5PW2K6 (gitlab-runner 2→3 replicas, namespace ci) had any downstream effect, rather than assuming it from timing.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

content.alerting:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
